findings.title: "Verified" claim that only file-level nodes carry `filePath` and `complexity` is false
findings.description:
Line 99 says nodes carrying `filePath` + `complexity` are "all `file`, `config`, `pipeline` — 238 total".

- In the real graph, `"filePath":` and `"complexity":` each occur 925 times, once per node.
- Function and class nodes carry both fields. For example, `function:src/squadron/providers/loader.py:ensure_provider_loaded` has a `filePath`.

Two statements built on this claim fail:
- The Correction 2 heading at line 143, "file-level means *carries a `filePath`*", is wrong. Every node carries one.
- The Correction 1 cross-check at lines 138-141 ("every `nodeIds` entry must resolve to a node carrying `filePath`") passes trivially for a function or class node, so it cannot detect drift. Only a type check can.
- The Correction 2 rule that "a node surviving this filter but carrying no `filePath` is reported as drift" (lines 160-161) cannot fire on this graph.

The selector itself (`type != function and != class`) is fine. Redefine "file-level" by type, and make the cross-check a type check.

findings.title: Tag and `languageNotes` figures use the 201-node `file` denominator the design itself rejects
findings.description:
The design says `entry-point` is on 27 nodes (line 104, and again at line 202). It says `languageNotes` covers 81/201, or 40% (line 105, and again at line 209). These counts cover `type == "file"` nodes only, but sections 3 and 4 operate on the 238 file-level nodes.

Against the real graph:
- `"entry-point"` appears 52 times in total. Per the sibling `understand.md` this is 24 function nodes plus 28 file-level nodes, not 27.
- `languageNotes` is present on 97 of 238 file-level nodes, about 41%, not 81/201.

This is the same silent narrowing that Correction 2 fixes, repeated in the design's own measurements. Re-measure on the 238-node set. Also note that function nodes carry the `entry-point` tag. That is a second reason the section 3 selection must be file-level-scoped.

findings.title: Section 6 contradicts itself, and its endpoint resolution is unspecified
findings.description:
Line 215 restricts inter-layer connections to `imports` and `depends_on`. Lines 218-220 then say "a `calls` edge between two functions in different layers still counts as an inter-layer signal". Only one of these can hold. In the real graph only 16 of 610 `imports`/`depends_on` edges touch a function or class endpoint, so the stated motivation is weak.

The design also does not say how a function or class endpoint is mapped to its owning file's layer.
- The sibling skill had to invent an id-prefix parse.
- The design has no rule for an endpoint that does not parse.
- The design has no rule for an endpoint whose file is in no layer.
- The design does not say whether such edges are dropped, reported, or flagged.

This path is exactly where silent miscounting would occur, and it also sits in tension with success criterion 9 (no function or class node is read).

Separately, `edges[].direction` is listed as a consumed field (line 88) but no section uses it. Drop it or say how it is used.

findings.title: Drift detection from the corrections has no stated disposition
Coverage reconciliation treats a mismatch as proof of an inconsistent graph, from one sample
findings.description:
`analyzedFiles == file-level node count` is established from one graph. The design then states that a mismatch "means the graph is internally inconsistent".

The architecture says upstream keeps `intermediate/scan-result.json` for incremental runs and has an `autoUpdate` setting (arch lines 87-88). `analyzedFiles` may legitimately count a subset after an incremental update. Other graphs can also contain non-file-level node types that the exclusion selector admits.

Reporting "inconsistent" would then be a false alarm to the reader. The Risk Assessment (lines 439-445) covers the corrections' dependence on one graph but not this one. Walkthrough step 1 (lines 364-365) also says to stop if the numbers disagree, even though a legitimately refreshed graph is the stated reason for re-running them. State a mismatch neutrally, with both numbers, and drop the "inconsistent" inference. Alternatively, say what upstream defines `analyzedFiles` to be.

findings.title: Section 7 contradicts itself on `.understandignore` and is thin on failure modes
findings.description:
- Line 234 says "An all-comments file (this repo's current state has 17 active lines) is reported as 'defaults only'". A file with 17 active lines is not all-comments. The parenthetical contradicts the rule.
- A missing `.understandignore` file gets a gap marker (line 180). A file with zero active patterns gets "defaults only". Semantically these are the same state for upstream, where the file is optional and defaults apply.
- Section 7 lists "the patterns" with no cap, although the file is user-edited and unbounded.
- Invalid JSON in `config.json`, and a `meta.json` that exists but lacks `analyzedFiles`, are not distinguished from "file unreadable".
- Reporting `config.json`'s `outputLanguage: en` gives a comprehension reader nothing about the codebase. The slice plan assigns nothing here, and it is cuttable.

findings.title: The per-section "closing observation" is an unspecified mechanism that breaks the no-inference rule
findings.description:
- Lines 245-250 require "the closing observation each section carries". It appears nowhere in the mapping table, which says each section "emits that fallback and nothing else" (line 170), and nowhere in the success criteria.
- The example given ("complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK") is not derivable from a complexity-by-layer table. It is the interpretive claim the rule forbids.
- The "mechanical" test is a judgment call, not a mechanical one.
- Criterion 8 and walkthrough step 2 check `grep -c INFERRED == 0`. That passes trivially for any prose that is never tagged, so it does not verify that inference was avoided.

Either cut the closing observation or define it as a specified field of each section. Give it a fallback, and give it a check that actually tests derivability.

findings.title: The `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` comparison misdescribes the document, and "unchanged" is not unchanged
findings.description:
- Line 266 says the template has a "ten-part structure (identity, architecture, build/test/deploy, code quality, security, performance, operations, and so on)". The reference file has eight sections: Identity & Stack, Architecture, Build/Test/Deploy, Code Quality & Defects, Issue Tracker & Project Health, AI Agent Integration, Risks & Recommendations, and Deep-Dive Plan. There is no security, performance, or operations section, and the file calls itself an "8-section structured analysis".
- The decision says "retain the document unchanged" (line 258) and then adds a cross-reference line to it (line 278).
- Criterion 11 calls the only changed "non-document files" `understand.md` plus a line in a file under `project-documents/`. That file is a document.

The conclusion (adopt the conventions, not the structure) still stands. Correct the factual description and reword the retention claim.

findings.title: The "mapping reused verbatim" by 363 omits fields 363 needs
findings.description:
The design promises 363 a per-section mapping to attempt first, reused "verbatim". The table is keyed to the seven analysis sections, not the concept sections.

- The architecture's concept mapping (arch lines 219-221) uses `tour[]` *node ordering* for Solution Approach, and `config` nodes for Initial Technical Direction and Development Approach.
- Section 5 here takes only `order`, `title` and `description`. It leaves out `tour[].nodeIds`, which the architecture says squadron should read as structured data (arch lines 101-105).
- No section consumes `config` nodes.

As written, 363 cannot attempt extraction for those concept sections from this mapping. Either add `tour[].nodeIds` to section 5 and state that 363 owns its own concept-section mapping, or soften "verbatim".

findings.title: Ordering and tie-break rules the table calls "binding" are incomplete
findings.description:
- Section 2 orders layers by descending count with no tie-breaker.
- Sections 3 and 4 say "then layer" without defining the layer order.
- Section 6 breaks ties by "weight", but edge `weight` is per edge. Whether the aggregate is a sum, a max or a mean is undefined.
- "Top ordinal tier" for hotspots is undefined when no node is `complex`. It is unclear whether the next tier then becomes the hotspots.
- A node lacking `complexity` or `summary` has no stated treatment, even though 361 anticipated such nodes.

Two runs could produce different documents from the same graph.

findings.title: Walkthrough steps 5-6 cannot run as written
findings.description:
- Step 5 creates `kg-empty-tour.json` and `kg-no-entrypoints.json`, and step 6 creates `meta-wrong.json`. The skill reads only `knowledge-graph.json` and `meta.json`, and nothing swaps the variants into place.
- `$S` is never defined.
- The scratch directory has no `project-documents/user/analysis/` to write into.
- `config.json` and `.understandignore` are not copied, so every scratch run emits unrelated section-7 gaps.
- Step 5 `cd`s into `.understand-anything`, and step 6 and step 8's `git diff` silently depend on the working directory.
- Step 2 hard-codes "expect 944" and says 943 exists. At this base commit `understand.md`, 943 and the graph are all absent (only 940-942 exist). 361's own walkthrough writes a new document on each of several runs, so the next index depends on how many documents were left behind.
- Spot-check 3 (the `.understandignore` count) reads the same file the skill reads, so it is not an independent check against the repo.

findings.title: Design size: restated material, an unplanned mechanism, and low-value checks
findings.description:
The plan rates this slice 3/5, Risk Low. Candidates to cut or defer:
- "Read discipline, unchanged" (lines 282-293) restates 361 and mainly narrates the widening that Correction 2 already covers.
- The "Interfaces Required" table (lines 75-88) duplicates the mapping table's source fields, and includes the unused `edges[].direction`.
- The closing-observation mechanism (see the earlier finding).
- `config.json` reporting (see the `.understandignore` finding).
- The `uv run ruff format --check .` step (line 430), since no Python changes.
- The long `[INFERRED]` and `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` rationale, which could be two short decision paragraphs.

findings.title: The 361 skill text that Correction 1 targets does not exist at this base commit
findings.description: `commands/analysis/understand.md`, `943-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` and `.understand-anything/` are all absent in this worktree. The claims about "the 361 skill states…" and "the generated `943` sample carries both wrong counts" cannot be checked here. The 361 design (`361-slice…md:108,244`) specifies `select(.type == "file" or ...)` and "file count" and says nothing about intersecting `nodeIds` with `type == "file"`, so the defect lives only in 361's implementation. The design is correctly sequenced after 361 (`dependencies: [361]`), but the corrections are defined against implementation text, not against the 361 design. State that 361 must be merged first and that the corrections are verified against the merged text.

findings.title: Boundaries, installer impact and arithmetic hold
findings.description:
- The design stays a skill-level markdown transform.
- `_install_prefix()` copies every `*.md` in the pack directory, so no installer or manifest change is needed.
- The existing `tests/skills/` tests pin only `tech-debt-audit.md`, so they are not disturbed.
- The staleness, hygiene and provenance contracts are untouched.
- The graph arithmetic reconciles: 476+211+201+20+17 = 925, and 925-238 = 687.
- The 13+4 config split and the 34/6 layer counts are consistent with each other.
- `src/squadron/data/pipelines/*.yaml` has 20 files, matching the pipeline node count.
- `meta.json` `analyzedFiles` is 238.
- `config.json` holds only `outputLanguage`.
- `.understandignore` has 17 active lines.
- `[GAP]` and the "never silently omitted" fallback rule follow the architecture's per-field resolution rule.
